title.narrative: A strategy implementing United Nations' Secretary General's Climate Action Priorities supporting full realization of the long-term goals of the Paris Agreement is developed and executed.

- availability of the strategy and evidence of its execution, including: - Global GHG emissions peak in 2025 and decline thereafter to be halved by 2023 - ODA eligible countries have an increased ability to adapt to the adverse impact of climate change and foster climate resilience and low greenhouse gas emissions development, in a manner that does not threaten food production. This is measured by the levels of funding and capacity building for adaptation projects in ODA eligible countries. - finance flows consistent with pathway toward net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and climate-resilient development.

target.value: - Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2030 emissions that are 10% lower than 2019 levels

actual.value: According to the UNFCCC NDCs Synthesis Report 2023, 20 Parties submitted new or updated NDCs between September 2022 and September 2023. 94% of Parties provided quantified mitigation targets, with 80% providing economy-wide targets. If these NDCs are fully implemented, total global GHG emissions (without the land use, land-use change, and forestry sector) in 2020 are estimated to be around 2.0% lower than 2019 levels.

target.value: -Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2030 emissions that are 20% lower than 2019 levels
-Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2030 emissions that are 40% lower than 2019 levels
-Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2030 emissions that are 45% lower than 2019 levels

- Global GHG emissions have peaked by 2025 and start declining - Adaptation needs are 90% covered in ODA eligible countries, especially through access to early warning systems. - Global financial flows are more aligned with 1.5C consistent net-zero pathways and cover needs for net zero transition especially ODA-eligble countries

title.narrative:
Scaled up adaptation and resilience finance and projects in dveloping countries including through cooperative initiatives such as the adaptation pipeline accelerator (APA), with CAT providing political guidance and oversight;
The SG's Early Warning Systems for all (EWS4ALL) initiative has expanded work on early warning systems in 30 underserved countries, with CAT political guidance and oversight, and in collaboration with other partners and initiatives.

target.value: - In 30 focus countries, the EWS4ALL initiative has been initiated starting to connect existing initiatives in the field with clear country-action plans and funding mechanism to finance the action plans. - APA initiative launched in 4 developing countries.
- Demonstrated progress of EW4ALL in 30 countries of first cohort with tangible improvements in EWS capabilities. - APA initiative expanded to 10 developing countries

actual.value:
EW4ALL has fully met its target, showing improvements in all 30 countries in the first cohort.
APA has made significant progress but has not yet reached the full expansion target.

target.value: -APA initiative expanded to 15 developing countries. -In additional 30 countries (cohort 3), the EWS4ALL initiative has been rolled-out connecting all existing initiatives in the field with clear country-action plans and funding mechanism to finance the action plans. Implementation progressing in 60 first and second cohort countries with tangible improvements in EWS capabilities.
-APA initiative expanded to 20 developing countries. -Globally all countries are covered by multi-hazard early warinng systems.

title.narrative: Output 1: High-level political advocacy to ensure more ambitious NDCs are submitted by countries to narrow the emissions gap facilitated.

Updated NDCs with increased of ambitious mitigation commitments and actions by the major emitters, particularly the G20 to ensure global peaking by 2025 and rapid decrease thereafter. Source of data for this indicator will be annual UNFCCC NDC synthesis report.

target.value: Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2023 emissions that are 10% lower than 2019 levels.

actual.value: NDCs submitted as of 25 September 2023 results in emissions that are 2% lower than 2019 levels.

target.value: Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2023 emissions that are 20% lower than 2019 levels

actual.value: Only 34 countries submitted new or updated NDCs between September 2023 and September 2024, resulting in almost no change in projected emissions reductions compared to 2019 levels.

target.value: Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2023 emissions that are 40% lower than 2019 levels
Updated NDCs submitted are expected to result in 2023 emissions that are 45% lower than 2019 levels
